transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nia Gomez (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (StratusWorks Sec PM), Marcus Hill (IT Ops), Ravi Kumar (Legal), Priya Shah (Cloud Arch)
Shared artifacts: CAIQ mapping spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.app/shared/caiq-stratusworks), SOC2 PDF (placeholder link), Evidence playbook deck (redwood.com/decks/evidence-playbook)

00:00 Avery (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Avery, AE on the account, Samir is our SE, Nia your CSM. The goal today is to walk through how we handle SIG/CAIQ and the evidence handoff so you can see what you'll need to collect.
00:18 Lena (StratusWorks): Thanks, yeah we want to understand the level of detail you provide. We have a vendor risk manager here doing the SIG and we need to fill in a couple of hundred rows.
00:27 Samir (Redwood SE): Great, we'll show the mapping and then the playbook for producing artifacts. Quick note up front, in some places transcription might say "K-V cash" cause the auto-transcript hates "KV cache" so please ignore weird words.
00:43 Marcus: Ha, noted. First question — SOC 2, do you have a Type II available and how current is it?
00:49 Avery: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II for the period ending Sep 30 2026. I'll upload the PDF to the shared folder after the call. It's our primary control baseline we reference in the CAIQ mapping.
01:03 Ravi (Legal): Is the SOC representative for both hosted and dedicated deployments or only hosted?
01:09 Samir: Good question. The SOC covers Redwood's hosted control plane and the managed hosted inference service. For Dedicated and Private there are control handoffs — we provide our internal controls and interface points but customer responsibility shifts for customer-managed infra. We'll call that out in the mapping.
01:30 Priya: On private deployments — our requirement is that logs remain in-region and keys are customer-managed. How do you support KMS?
01:38 Samir: Two patterns: 1) Redwood-managed keys (we use cloud KMS with HSM-backed key material) or 2) Bring-your-own-key (BYOK) where you provision a customer-managed KMS key and we integrate via IAM policies and key wrapping. For on-prem you can supply an HSM or KMS endpoint. We also document KMS key lifecycle and rotation in the evidence pack.
02:05 Lena: Can you provide redaction guidance? Some of our logs can't contain PII.
02:11 Samir: Absolutely — our sample audit logs are anonymized. We also provide a mapping of which fields are redacted and a schema for the log export. I'll attach a sample CSV and a JSON event sample in the follow-up.
02:28 Marcus: How long are logs retained by default? We have to prove retention for X years depending on our regulators.
02:34 Avery: Default retention in hosted is 90 days, with paid retention add-ons to 7 years. For Dedicated and Private you control retention via the storage config. We can add a note in the SIG mapping showing retention tiers and how to request extended retention.
02:54 Ravi: On encryption in transit and at rest — do you use customer certs or do you terminate at your load balancer?
03:00 Samir: TLS termination is configurable. Hosted terminates at our edge with certs managed by Redwood. If you require end-to-end we can support TLS passthrough to private endpoints in VPC or mutual TLS to customer gateways. For at-rest, we encrypt with KMS-managed keys (as discussed).
03:20 Lena: On RBAC and SSO — we use Okta. How granular is your RBAC? Can we map to our internal roles?
03:26 Samir: We support SAML v2 and OIDC SSO, and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based and can be mapped to groups coming from your IdP — we have admin/ops/viewer/readonly roles by default and you can define custom roles for dedicated tenants. We'll share a sample SCIM group-to-role mapping.
03:48 Priya: Do you provide audit logs for admin actions (who changed a config, who triggered a model deploy)?
03:53 Samir: Yes — admin audit trails include user, action, timestamp, IP, and request id. We can surface them in the console and export them. Our sample will include anonymized change events.
04:10 Lena: For the SIG, the control owner wants screenshots for RBAC settings and an exported user list. Is that something you can supply?
04:16 Samir: Yes, screenshot artifacts, config snippets, and exported lists are part of the playbook where possible. For customer-managed infra we'll show the configuration points to verify customer responsibilities.
04:30 Marcus: A few controls ask about data residency. We are EU-only for some workloads — can Redwood guarantee region locking?
04:37 Avery: Yes, we support region pinning in both Hosted (by routing to EU region) and Dedicated (capacity deployed in region). For Private deployments on-prem or VPC the data never leaves the customer region unless you configure replication. We'll put language in the mapping to indicate the residency guarantee per deployment mode.
04:55 Ravi: Security questionnaires sometimes want very specific answers like "Do you have MFA for console access?" — what level of specificity do you provide in the SIG cells?
05:01 Nia (Redwood CSM): We aim to provide clear answers with evidentiary artifacts. For MFA we typically say "Yes — MFA enforced for all interactive console access" and attach a screenshot of the access policy and a policy doc. If you need more specific legal-level wording we can collaborate with your legal team for final phrasing.
05:20 Lena: Great. Okay I want to dig into one of the CAIQ controls — there's a long section around key management. I see you have a CAIQ mapping but some rows are blank. Can we walk an example?
05:29 Samir: Sure — open the spreadsheet. Row 122 is the KMS customer key control. Our mapping for hosted says "partially implemented" because we offer Redwood-managed KMS by default; BYOK is supported via remote wrapping. For Dedicated it's customer optional. For Private it's customer-managed. The evidence we attach differs per case — for hosted, we'll include KMS configuration screenshots and key policy excerpts; for BYOK we'll include key policy acceptance procedure.
06:02 Priya: For BYOK — do you support key rotation initiated from customer side, or does Redwood rotate?
06:08 Samir: For BYOK the customer controls rotation. Redwood supports rotation scheduling but will not rotate customer-managed keys unless expressly authorized. We can provide a key rotation playbook sample.
06:22 Marcus: Another item — network-level logs and flow logs. Do you have VPC flow logs for Dedicated?
06:27 Samir: Yes, Dedicated offers VPC flow logs; for Hosted we capture network telemetry at edge but customers generally ask us to provide flow log exports to their audit bucket. For Private, flow logs live in your environment.
06:42 Lena: When the questionnaires ask "Describe the encryption key lifecycle" what's the expected level of detail? Some auditors want KMS ARN, rotation schedule, who has access, HSM attestations, etc.
06:53 Samir: We provide a standard text that covers key lifecycle — creation, use, rotation, revocation, backup — and append a KMS policy snippet and HSM vendor attestation if applicable. We can include the ARN pattern for hosted keys and a sample IAM policy that shows separation of duties.
07:18 Ravi: Compliance evidence — do you accept statements of fact or do you insist on logs and screenshots? Some regulators prefer logs over a written assertion.
07:26 Avery: We try to provide primary artifacts where possible: PDFs of reports, screenshots, exported logs, IAM policy snippets. For certain controls we'll provide an attestation letter if the primary artifact isn't feasible. We also tag each SIG cell with the artifact type so you know whether it's "policy", "screenshot", "log", or "third-party report".
07:44 Priya: For log formats — do you provide JSON events or CSV lines? Our SIEM expects JSON.
07:50 Samir: We can export logs as JSON (structured events) with a documented schema. We'll include a sample JSON event and field descriptions.
08:03 Lena: A weird one — some questionnaires ask if you use "KV cache" for session state. I assume that's the inference runtime detail — are you able to answer?
08:10 Samir: Yes, we use a KV cache for decoder state for model performance; in the SIG we give a high-level answer about state retention and TTLs. Sorry again if the transcript munges it to "K-V cash" earlier.
08:26 Marcus: For the evidence handoff — do you provide a single zip with everything or a per-control link set?
08:31 Nia: We typically provide a per-control mapping in the CAIQ spreadsheet with links to artifacts in a secure share. For larger customers we can set up a temporary S3 bucket or a managed share with short-lived URLs and an index file.
08:44 Ravi: Who signs off on the evidence? Do you have a delegated evidence owner?
08:49 Avery: Our security operations team own the artifacts. I'll include a contact list with ownership for each artifact (e.g., SOC2 -> Security Ops; KMS policy -> Infra team).
09:02 Priya: Does Redwood support proof of key deletion / key destruction?
09:07 Samir: For customer-managed keys you can provide deletion logs from your KMS. For Redwood-managed keys we can provide key lifecycle events and deletion attestations in the audit trail. If you need a formal COA (certificate of destruction) that's handled case-by-case and we'd route to Security Compliance.
09:28 Lena: Question from our risk team — they want to know frequency of vulnerability scanning, penetration tests, and whether you share pentest reports.
09:35 Samir: We do internal vulnerability scans weekly with authenticated scans monthly, and engage a third party for annual pen tests. We can supply a redacted executive summary of the latest pen test and a letter of attestation. Full raw reports are sometimes restricted but we can share aggregated remediation timelines.
09:58 Marcus: About SLA claims — some of our developers asked how you'd show availability metrics as evidence.
10:04 Nia: We provide uptime dashboards and can export 3 months of per-route latency/availability metrics. For contractual SLAs we include a metrics export and incident reports as evidence.
10:19 Ravi: This is helpful. Let's talk about the process — if we hand you the SIG with blanks, how long until you can populate the cells?
10:26 Avery: It depends on the scope. For a first pass on high-priority 50 rows we can usually fill in 5-7 business days, longer if we need legal review on phrasing. For full questionnaires with many custom legal asks we coordinate with Security and Legal which can add 2-3 weeks.
10:44 Lena: Is there any part of the SIG you typically decline to answer? e.g., "provide service account passwords" — obviously not.
10:50 Samir: Yes, we never provide secrets like passwords or private keys. For operational access requests we provide sanitized artifacts and access logs.
11:02 Priya: Can we get a short sample of an evidence index?
11:07 Nia: I'll drop a short exemplar after the call — it's just a table: control id, redwood answer, artifact type, artifact link, evidence owner.
11:21 Marcus: A few technical things — can you support TLS mutual auth for model serving endpoints for mutual-TLS?
11:26 Samir: Yes for Private we can support mTLS. For Hosted we can do mutual auth to customer gateways or VPN tunnels depending on architecture. We'll cover the exact flow in the technical deep-dive.
11:40 Lena: Okay last section, legal phrasing — sometimes your default language in the CAIQ feels aspirational. Will Redwood engage on redlining answers?
11:48 Avery: We're open to working through phrasing with legal for enterprise contracts. We'll flag any language that is a security or compliance boundary and propose alternate wordings.
11:58 Ravi: Good. Can you add a line in the mapping for residual risk when a control is shared responsibility?
12:03 Samir: Yep — each row includes a "responsibility" column: Redwood, Customer, or Shared, plus a short residual risk note.
12:18 Lena: Thanks — this was very useful. Quick recap of next steps?
12:24 Avery: Recap: We'll upload SOC2 PDF, CAIQ mapping link, sample logs and KMS policy snippets. Samir prepares anonymized logs; Nia will send a follow-up invite for the Jan technical deep-dive. You (StratusWorks) will return prioritized SIG rows for the critical controls by Jan 4.
12:43 Marcus: Sounds good. One last ask — can we get an example of the SCIM group mapping?
12:48 Samir: I'll include a SCIM group-to-role example in the shared folder.
12:55 Lena: Great thanks everyone.
13:00 Avery: Thanks all, we'll send notes and follow-ups.

End of transcript.

Meeting recap (automated):

- Agreed artifacts: SOC2, CAIQ mapping, anonymized logs, KMS policy snippets, RBAC screenshots, SCIM mapping.
- Next meeting: Technical deep-dive week of 2027-01-11 (Samir to lead).

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcription occasionally garbled technical terms (KV cache, KMS/HSM) and speaker labels; content reviewed by Redwood AE for accuracy.
